title: Rabies Risk Exposes Dog-Trade Gaps; Abolition Needed by 2030
excerpt: Rabies leaves no room for uninspected animal movement. Protecting Vietnamese families and pets requires traceable supply chains—and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
One bite can start a race against death. Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters broken skin or mucous membranes; once clinical symptoms appear, disease is virtually 100% fatal. That public-health reality makes uninspected animal movement and slaughter a biosecurity failure—not a matter settled by calling trade “tradition.”

Household exposure and commercial supply chains are separate risks. A bite or scratch demands immediate wound washing and urgent medical assessment. Secret transport and slaughter create different hazards: weak traceability, uncertain vaccination status, and failures of veterinary inspection. Neither risk proves every animal in trade carries rabies. Both show why enforcement cannot depend on trust alone.

“Farm-raised” needs records, not slogans

Farm-raised claims require verifiable records: lawful origin, ownership, vaccination, transport documents, quarantine controls, and inspection. No such claim should erase the need for proof. When animals move without reliable traceability, stolen family companions and illegally sourced animals become harder to detect. That burden falls on Vietnamese families protecting pets, not on criminal operators seeking profit.

Health response cannot wait

After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical care for vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or an approved monoclonal antibody. Post-exposure prophylaxis must begin before symptoms develop. World Health Organization guidance confirms the urgency.

Vietnamese communities deserve safe streets, honest inspection, and protection from pet theft. Public-health targets and enforcement programs matter, but SDE demands a clear final safeguard: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
